### Top sellers

Circana has revealed the best-selling games of 2024 overall in the US. Call of

CFB 25, meanwhile, was No. 2 for 2024 overall, and ranked No. 1 on Xbox
platforms. It is now the best-selling sports video game in US history.

The reporting period for the charts below covers December 30, 2023 through
January 4, 2025. Read on to see the top 20 best-selling games of 2024 so far.

data from many publishers, but not all (Nintendo does not share digital data,
for example). These rankings also do not include add-on content and
microtransaction revenue.

_**Call of Duty: Black Ops 6**_ is a 2024 [first-person shooter](/wiki/First-
person_shooter "First-person shooter") [video game](/wiki/Video_game "Video
game") co-developed by [Treyarch](/wiki/Treyarch "Treyarch") and [Raven
Software](/wiki/Raven_Software "Raven Software") and published by
[Activision](/wiki/Activision "Activision"). It is the twenty-first
installment of the _[Call of Duty](/wiki/Call_of_Duty "Call of Duty")_ series
and is the seventh main entry in the [_Black
Ops_](/wiki/Call_of_Duty#Black_Ops_story_arc "Call of Duty") sub-series,
following _[Call of Duty: Black Ops Cold
War](/wiki/Call_of_Duty:_Black_Ops_Cold_War "Call of Duty: Black Ops Cold
War")_ (2020). Set during [Operation Desert Storm](/wiki/Gulf_War "Gulf War"),
_Black Ops 6_ 's [single-player](/wiki/Single-player "Single-player") story
follows rogue [CIA](/wiki/Central_Intelligence_Agency "Central Intelligence
Agency") operatives Troy Marshall and Frank Woods as they assemble a team of
agents to hunt down Pantheon, a [paramilitary](/wiki/Paramilitary
"Paramilitary") group with covert ties to the agency. As with previous _Call
of Duty_ titles, the game also includes a [multiplayer](/wiki/Multiplayer
"Multiplayer") component and the [cooperative](/wiki/Cooperative_video_game
"Cooperative video game") round-based [Zombies
mode](/wiki/Call_of_Duty_Zombies "Call of Duty Zombies").

_Black Ops 6_ had a four-year development cycle—the longest in _Call of Duty_
history; a portion of the game's production was spent on rebuilding core
aspects of _Black Ops_ within the latest version of the _Call of Duty_ [game
engine](/wiki/Game_engine "Game engine"). An omnidirectional movement system
was also introduced, allowing players to sprint, dive, and slide in any
direction. Marketing for _Black Ops 6_ began in May 2024, through the release
of [live-action](/wiki/Live-action "Live-action") teaser trailers and the
publishing of advertisements on the front pages of multiple newspaper outlets;
a full reveal debuted during the 2024 [Xbox Games
Showcase](/wiki/Xbox_Developer_Direct "Xbox Developer Direct") event on June
9. The game was released on October 25, 2024, for [PlayStation
4](/wiki/PlayStation_4 "PlayStation 4"), [PlayStation 5](/wiki/PlayStation_5
"PlayStation 5"), [Windows](/wiki/Windows "Windows"), [Xbox
One](/wiki/Xbox_One "Xbox One"), and [Xbox Series
X/S](/wiki/Xbox_Series_X_and_Series_S "Xbox Series X and Series S").

Upon release, _Black Ops 6_ received generally favorable reviews from critics,
achieved the largest launch weekend in the franchise's history, and was
nominated for several accolades. All three modes were met with praise, with
critics positively highlighting the new omnidirectional movement system. A
sequel, titled _[Call of Duty: Black Ops 7](/wiki/Call_of_Duty:_Black_Ops_7
"Call of Duty: Black Ops 7")_ , was released on November 14, 2025.

## Gameplay

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Call_of_Duty:_Black_Ops_6&action=edit&section=1
"Edit section: Gameplay")]

[![A visual demonstration of the omnidirectional movement system featured in
Call of Duty: Black Ops 6. The demonstration depicts the game's
omnidirectional sprinting
ability.](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/9/96/Black_Ops_6_Omnimovement.gif/250px-
Black_Ops_6_Omnimovement.gif)](/wiki/File:Black_Ops_6_Omnimovement.gif)New to
_Call of Duty: Black Ops 6_ is omnidirectional movement, allowing players to
sprint, dive, and slide in any direction. The above clip demonstrates the
omnidirectional sprinting ability.

_Call of Duty: Black Ops 6_ is a [first-person shooter](/wiki/First-
person_shooter "First-person shooter").[3] Depending on the [game
mode](/wiki/Game_mode "Game mode") selected, players use a selection of
military equipment, such as weapons, "field upgrades", and "scorestreaks", to
combat AI opponents, other human players, or [undead creatures](/wiki/Zombie
"Zombie").[3][4][5] Players can perform a wide variety of movement actions
when traversing a [level/map](/wiki/Level_\(video_games\) "Level \(video
games\)"), including walking, crouching, sprinting, jumping, sliding, and
diving;[6] they can also perform a "Tactical Sprint", which further increases
the player's movement speed for a limited duration.[7] In a change from
previous _[Call of Duty](/wiki/Call_of_Duty "Call of Duty")_ titles, players
have omnidirectional control over the sprint, dive, and slide mechanics,
allowing them to perform these actions in any direction; players can also
rotate themselves in a 360 degree view while they are laying in the [prone
position](/wiki/Prone_position "Prone position").[1] In addition, a series of
"Intelligent Movement" settings are also available to players, which automate
certain movement actions, including sprinting and mantling.[8]

_Black Ops 6_ features three main game modes: a [single-player](/wiki/Single-
player "Single-player") campaign, a [multiplayer](/wiki/Multiplayer
"Multiplayer") component and the cooperative round-based [Zombies
mode](/wiki/Call_of_Duty_Zombies "Call of Duty Zombies").[2] In the campaign,
players assume control of a [silent protagonist](/wiki/Silent_protagonist
"Silent protagonist"), "Case", as he and a team of rogue
[CIA](/wiki/Central_Intelligence_Agency "Central Intelligence Agency")
operatives work to hunt down "Pantheon", a [paramilitary](/wiki/Paramilitary
"Paramilitary") group with covert ties to the agency.[9] The campaign features
11 missions,[10] and is estimated to take at least 8 hours to complete.[11]
Players typically have multiple ways to approach a mission's objectives; some
missions include [stealth](/wiki/Stealth_game "Stealth game") elements.[9] In-
between missions, players are able to access a [safe house](/wiki/Safe_house
"Safe house"), where they can select new missions via an [evidence
board](/wiki/Evidence_board "Evidence board"), interact with [non-player
characters](/wiki/Non-player_character "Non-player character") (NPCs),[1] and
spend cash, which is found throughout missions, on various in-game perks;
these are split across three categories, which are related to the player's
physical abilities, weapons, and gear.[9] Certain campaign missions reward
players with cosmetic items for use in the multiplayer and Zombies modes upon
their completion, including weapon "blueprints", player skins,
[stickers](/wiki/Sticker "Sticker"), and weapon charms.[12]

The multiplayer component puts two teams of six—split across the "Rogue Black
Ops" and "Crimson One" factions—against each other across a wide selection of
game modes,[13] such as "[Team
Deathmatch](/wiki/Deathmatch_\(video_games\)#Variations "Deathmatch \(video
games\)")", "Domination", "Hardpoint", and "Kill Order"; an exception to this
is the round-based "Gunfight" mode, which puts two teams of two on small-sized
maps with randomized loadouts.[14] Like previous _Call of Duty_ games, player
performance is tracked with [experience points](/wiki/Experience_point
"Experience point") (XP), which is earned by killing enemy players, completing
objectives, or finishing challenges;[15] XP can also be earned in the Zombies
mode.[16] As players rank up, they gain access to various loadout items,
including new weapons, pieces of equipment, and perks, the latter of which are
split into three "combat specialties": "Enforcer", "Recon", and "Strategist".
Selecting three perks of the same specialty grants access to in-game buffs;
for example, if a player has three "Strategist" perks equipped, they will be
able to see enemy equipment through walls and deploy equipment faster.[17]
Once players reach level 55, they can choose to enter the "Prestige" ranking
system, which resets their progress back to level 1 but grants a set of
cosmetic rewards and a token that can be used to permanently unlock any
loadout item. This process can be done up to ten times; once players complete
the tenth Prestige, they become a "Prestige Master" and are granted the
ability to rank up to level 1000, and if they do so, they become a "Prestige
Legend" and receive additional cosmetic items.[18]

In Zombies, one to four players fight endless hordes of the undead, which
increase in both number and difficulty with every completed round,[19] across
six maps: "Liberty Falls", "Terminus", "Citadelle des Morts", "The Tomb",
"Shattered Veil", and "Reckoning".[20] Each map includes a main quest that
players must solve on their own, along with a number of side quests and
[easter eggs](/wiki/Easter_egg_\(media\) "Easter egg \(media\)").[21] Two
additional modes—"Directed" and "Grief"—were added to all maps post-
launch;[22][23] the former allows players to complete main quests with in-game
assistance,[22] while the latter pits two teams of four players against one
another as they attempt to survive the undead, while hindering the enemy team
indirectly via debuffs.[23] Zombies features two primary currencies for
players to manage: "Essence" and "Salvage"; Essence is used to unlock access
to new parts of the maps, acquire weapon upgrades from the "Pack-a-Punch"
machine, and to purchase additional player upgrades, including "Perk-a-Cola"
cans and [armor vests](/wiki/Body_armor "Body armor"), while Salvage is used
to acquire ammo modifications for the player's weapons, increase a weapon's
damage tier, and to craft various pieces of lethal and tactical equipment.[21]
Players are also able to obtain "GobbleGums"—single-use consumables that grant
various in-game effects—and unlock "Augments", a set of minor and major
upgrades to perks, field upgrades and ammo mods. Each perk, field upgrade, and
ammo mod features up to three minor and major Augments, with one of each type
being equipable at the same time, allowing players to customize and experiment
with different play styles.[19]

### Campaign

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Call_of_Duty:_Black_Ops_6&action=edit&section=3
"Edit section: Campaign")]

In January 1991, amidst the start of [Operation Desert Storm](/wiki/Gulf_War
"Gulf War"), CIA operatives Troy Marshall ([Y'lan Noel](/wiki/Y%27lan_Noel
"Y'lan Noel")) and William "Case" Calderon, along with their handler,
Operations Specialist Jane Harrow ([Dawn Olivieri](/wiki/Dawn_Olivieri "Dawn
Olivieri")), are deployed to the [Iraq–Kuwait
border](/wiki/Iraq%E2%80%93Kuwait_border "Iraq–Kuwait border") to extract
Iraqi [minister of
defence](/wiki/Ministry_of_Defence_\(Iraq\)#Minister_of_defence "Ministry of
Defence \(Iraq\)") Saeed Alawi (Jordan Bielsky), but are forced to go off
mission when Alawi claims to be targeted by a rogue paramilitary force called
"Pantheon". After surviving an encounter with Pantheon forces, the team
prepares to extract Alawi, but he is executed by Russell Adler ([Bruce
Thomas](/wiki/Bruce_Thomas_\(actor\) "Bruce Thomas \(actor\)")), a rogue agent
who fled from the CIA after he was framed as a mole for the
[Nicaraguan](/wiki/Nicaragua "Nicaragua") drug lord Raul Menendez. Adler
allows himself to be captured, telling Marshall to relay a message to fellow
operative Frank Woods (Damon Victor Allen): "Bishop takes Rook". Afterwards,
[CIA Deputy Director](/wiki/Deputy_Director_of_the_Central_Intelligence_Agency
"Deputy Director of the Central Intelligence Agency") Daniel Livingstone ([Lou
Diamond Phillips](/wiki/Lou_Diamond_Phillips "Lou Diamond Phillips"))
reprimands the team for Alawi's death, ignores their warnings about Pantheon,
and suspends Woods, Marshall, and Case from duty.

Woods reveals to Marshall that Adler's message refers to an abandoned
[KGB](/wiki/KGB "KGB") safe house in [Bulgaria](/wiki/Bulgaria
"Bulgaria")—code-named "the Rook"—that the two discovered in 1976, and decides
to go there with Marshall and Case to investigate Pantheon; Harrow stays
behind to cover for their absence. After using Adler's files to recruit
ex-[Stasi](/wiki/Stasi "Stasi") technical genius Felix Neumann ([Seamus
Dever](/wiki/Seamus_Dever "Seamus Dever")) and assassin Sevati "Sev" Dumas
([Karen David](/wiki/Karen_David "Karen David")), the team moves to break
Adler out of a CIA [black site](/wiki/Black_site "Black site") hidden under
[Washington, D.C.](/wiki/Washington,_D.C. "Washington, D.C."), while a
political event hosted by Governor [Bill Clinton](/wiki/Bill_Clinton "Bill
Clinton") ([Jim Meskimen](/wiki/Jim_Meskimen "Jim Meskimen")) takes place
above ground. The team extracts Adler just as Pantheon assaults the black
site, but they are blamed for the attack instead and are declared fugitives.
Adler reveals that Pantheon has been engaging in weapons deals with [Saddam
Hussein](/wiki/Saddam_Hussein "Saddam Hussein"); with the help of
[MI6](/wiki/MI6 "MI6") agent Helen Park ([Lily Cowles](/wiki/Lily_Cowles "Lily
Cowles")) and allied [SAS](/wiki/Special_Air_Service "Special Air Service")
forces, the team assaults one of Hussein's palaces in western Iraq, where they
find "the Cradle", a [psychochemical weapon](/wiki/Psychochemical_warfare
"Psychochemical warfare") that originated from an abandoned CIA biolab in
[Kentucky](/wiki/Kentucky "Kentucky").

While Adler stays behind to track down Pantheon's head scientist, Matvey Gusev
([Yuri Lowenthal](/wiki/Yuri_Lowenthal "Yuri Lowenthal")), Case, Marshall, and
Sev investigate the biolab. Case accidentally inhales Cradle gas and
hallucinates fighting off [undead creatures](/wiki/Zombie "Zombie") while
hearing a woman's voice, which explains that Pantheon was originally a secret
CIA division overseeing Cradle's development as a [performance-enhancing
drug](/wiki/Performance-enhancing_substance "Performance-enhancing
substance"), with Case being the only test subject, before Livingstone shut
down the project and disbanded Pantheon. When Case regains his senses, the
team discovers that Pantheon has already stolen the biolab's stores of Cradle,
and also find a recording revealing that Harrow is working with Pantheon.
Using clues in the recording, the team steals financial records from a casino
in the European principality of Avalon, which reveal that the casino had been
wiring money to Gusev in Iraq. Afterwards, Case and Marshall reunite with
Adler in Kuwait and work with his old ally, [U.S.
Army](/wiki/United_States_Army "United States Army") Captain Lawrence Sims
(Reggie Watkins), to capture Gusev, who reveals that the Cradle is being
stored in [Vorkuta](/wiki/Vorkutlag "Vorkutlag").

The team raids Vorkuta, and while they are unable to stop the Cradle from
being moved, they capture Harrow and bring her to the Rook for interrogation.
Adler injects Harrow with a truth serum, prompting her to reveal that she
joined Pantheon after they leaked information claiming that Adler killed her
parents, and that Pantheon is planning to use the Cradle to carry out a [false
flag attack](/wiki/False_flag "False flag") on the [Capitol
Building](/wiki/United_States_Capitol "United States Capitol") to discredit
Livingstone and replace him with Harrow, putting them in control of the CIA.
Pantheon forces assault the Rook and rescue Harrow; Case gives chase and
boards Harrow's escape helicopter, causing it to crash in a near-by river.
Under the influence of released Cradle gas, Case strangles Harrow to death
before presumably drowning. Marshall tries to radio Case, explaining that
Livingstone managed to evacuate the Capitol. Two weeks later, the team meets
with Livingstone, who asks them to continue working as an independent
clandestine unit in order to eradicate Pantheon and its true leaders, who are
conducting operations in Avalon. Meanwhile, Pantheon operative Jackson Caine
([Rick Pasqualone](/wiki/Rick_Pasqualone "Rick Pasqualone")) infiltrates
Livingstone's office and accesses his computer.

### Multiplayer

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Call_of_Duty:_Black_Ops_6&action=edit&section=4
"Edit section: Multiplayer")]

In December 1991, the Rogue Black Ops team—led by Sev and Marshall—establishes
an alliance with a local Avalonian crime family, the French Syndicate, to
attack their rival and Pantheon ally, the Luttazzi Family.[24] Following
several successful operations, Sev is attacked by "Nocturne", an assassin who
is looking to collect a bounty placed on her by the Luttazzi, though she
manages to escape.[25]

Several days later, Woods provides Adler with a case file and VHS tape that
was sent to the former by late CIA agent Jason Hudson, some time following his
death in December 1989;[b][26] the tape reveals that Pantheon was involved in
various CIA activities during the [Vietnam War](/wiki/Vietnam_War "Vietnam
War") and the [Soviet–Afghan War](/wiki/Soviet%E2%80%93Afghan_War
"Soviet–Afghan War").[27] Using Hudson's case file, the Rogue team discovers a
list of every Pantheon agent's code name, but find that it's encrypted using a
Soviet-era cipher;[28] this prompts the team to assault a CIA black site in
[Iceland](/wiki/Iceland "Iceland") to free Vikhor "Stitch" Kuzmin ([Chris
Parson](/wiki/Chris_Parson "Chris Parson")), the former leader of the [Perseus
spy ring](/wiki/Perseus_\(spy\) "Perseus \(spy\)") who was captured by Adler
in August 1984.[c][29] With Stitch's help, the Rogue team decrypts the code
names and forces Pantheon's agents out of hiding.[30] While Adler, Woods, and
Marshall return to the U.S. to receive a pardon and a full arsenal of weaponry
and support to hunt down the remaining loose Pantheon agents,[31] Sev chooses
to stay in Avalon to unite its criminal factions.[30] By 2035, she helped turn
one such faction, "The Guild", into a global technology corporation;[d] a
[monument](/wiki/Monument "Monument") to her is placed at a Guild factory in
[Tokyo Bay](/wiki/Tokyo_Bay "Tokyo Bay").[32]

## Development

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Call_of_Duty:_Black_Ops_6&action=edit&section=6
"Edit section: Development")]

[Treyarch](/wiki/Treyarch "Treyarch") and [Raven
Software](/wiki/Raven_Software "Raven Software") co-developed _Black Ops 6_ ,
with Raven leading production on the game's single-player campaign and
Treyarch developing the multiplayer and Zombies modes.[33] Activision Central
Design, Activision Central Technology, Activision Shanghai,
[Beenox](/wiki/Beenox "Beenox"), [Demonware](/wiki/Demonware "Demonware"),
[High Moon Studios](/wiki/High_Moon_Studios "High Moon Studios"), [Infinity
Ward](/wiki/Infinity_Ward "Infinity Ward"), and [Sledgehammer
Games](/wiki/Sledgehammer_Games "Sledgehammer Games") provided additional
development work on the title, with Beenox also leading work on the
[Windows](/wiki/Windows "Windows") version.[1] The game boasts a four-year
development cycle,[34] the longest in _Call of Duty_ history,[35] and entered
[play-testing](/wiki/Playtest "Playtest") in 2022.[36] According to associate
design director Matt Scronce, the extended production allowed the developers
to be "very intentional about what it means to be a _Black Ops_ game" and to
re-examine key features, including visual fidelity, movement, and campaign
design;[34] they also re-added several fan-favorite features from previous
_Call of Duty_ titles that had been absent from recent entries, including the
"Prestige" ranking system and the "Theater" mode,[37] which allows players to
rewatch their previous multiplayer matches.[38]

_Black Ops 6_ is built on _Call of Duty_ 's "shared" [game
engine](/wiki/Game_engine "Game engine"), first introduced in _[Call of Duty:
Modern Warfare II](/wiki/Call_of_Duty:_Modern_Warfare_II_\(2022_video_game\)
"Call of Duty: Modern Warfare II \(2022 video game\)")_ (2022); previous
Treyarch titles used a separate engine developed at the studio. A portion of
the game's four-year development was spent on rebuilding "the core _Black Ops_
experience" from the ground-up within the new engine and ensuring that the
multiplayer mode "[felt] like _Black Ops_."[39] Treyarch also overhauled the
[user interface](/wiki/User_interface "User interface") for the _Call of Duty
HQ_ launcher—a hub for accessing the latest _Call of Duty_ titles and _[Call
of Duty: Warzone](/wiki/Call_of_Duty:_Warzone_\(2022_video_game\) "Call of
Duty: Warzone \(2022 video game\)")_ —to address design issues found in
_Modern Warfare II_ and _[Call of Duty: Modern Warfare
III](/wiki/Call_of_Duty:_Modern_Warfare_III_\(2023_video_game\) "Call of Duty:
Modern Warfare III \(2023 video game\)")_ (2023) and to provide players with
direct access to titles within _Call of Duty HQ_.[40]

### Music

"Edit section: Music")]

[![An image of Jack Wall, the lead composer for Call of Duty: Black Ops
6.](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f7/Jack_Wall_by_Gage_Skidmore.jpg/250px-
Jack_Wall_by_Gage_Skidmore.jpg)](/wiki/File:Jack_Wall_by_Gage_Skidmore.jpg)[Jack
Wall](/wiki/Jack_Wall_\(composer\) "Jack Wall \(composer\)") (pictured)
composed the score for _Black Ops 6_.[41]

[Jack Wall](/wiki/Jack_Wall_\(composer\) "Jack Wall \(composer\)") composed
the music for _Black Ops 6_ , as he had done for every entry in the sub-series
since _[Call of Duty: Black Ops II](/wiki/Call_of_Duty:_Black_Ops_II "Call of
Duty: Black Ops II")_ (2012).[41] Jim Lordeman, [Jimmy
Hinson](/wiki/Big_Giant_Circles "Big Giant Circles"), and Canadian rock duo
[Romes](/wiki/Romes_\(band\) "Romes \(band\)") provided additional music; Wall
collaborated with Hinson and Romes on the main theme song for the game's
multiplayer,[42] titled "Raining the Fire".[41] Additionally, Kevin Sherwood
composed original songs for every _Black Ops 6_ Zombies map, which are hidden
as [easter eggs](/wiki/Easter_egg_\(media\) "Easter egg \(media\)") within the
maps. Each map's song features a unique voicalist; notable singers include
[Cristina Scabbia](/wiki/Cristina_Scabbia "Cristina Scabbia"), [Matt
Heafy](/wiki/Matt_Heafy "Matt Heafy"), [Malukah](/wiki/Malukah "Malukah"), and
Elena Siegman.[43]

Wall started working on _Black Ops 6_ 's score near the end of March 2024;[44]
he initially worked on one of the game's levels, "The Cradle", in order to
allow the development team to implement his music as a [proof-of-
concept](/wiki/Proof-of-concept "Proof-of-concept"), before moving to write
the game's main theme, feeling that if he went "too far without a theme, it's
going to feel like nothing's really connected";[42] once he completed the
theme, the score began to "[fall] into place". Wall sought to incorporate the
[grunge](/wiki/Grunge "Grunge") sound of the early 1990s—the era in which the
game is set in—and combine it with his orchestral and synth work;[41] after
listening to some of their work on [Instagram](/wiki/Instagram
"Instagram"),[42] he reached out to Romes and asked them to help "fuck up"
some score tracks for the game with "snarling guitar[s] and thundering
drums".[41]

## Release

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Call_of_Duty:_Black_Ops_6&action=edit&section=9
"Edit section: Release")]

_Black Ops 6_ was released on October 25, 2024, for [PlayStation
4](/wiki/PlayStation_4 "PlayStation 4"), [PlayStation 5](/wiki/PlayStation_5
"PlayStation 5"), [Windows](/wiki/Windows "Windows"), [Xbox
One](/wiki/Xbox_One "Xbox One"), and [Xbox Series
X/S](/wiki/Xbox_Series_X_and_Series_S "Xbox Series X and Series S").[63] The
title was made available to subscribers of select [Xbox Game
Pass](/wiki/Xbox_Game_Pass "Xbox Game Pass") plans on release day, including
Xbox Game Pass Ultimate, PC Game Pass and Xbox Game Pass for Console.[64] It
is also available on select [cloud gaming](/wiki/Cloud_gaming "Cloud gaming")
platforms, including [GeForce Now](/wiki/GeForce_Now "GeForce Now") and [Xbox
Cloud Gaming](/wiki/Xbox_Cloud_Gaming "Xbox Cloud Gaming").[65][66] The game
requires a continuous internet connection to play all of its modes, including
the single-player campaign; Activision has stated that the requirement is due
to a texture streaming feature, which is used to ensure the best possible
visual quality without significantly increasing the game's file size.[67]
_Black Ops 6_ was blocked from sale in [Kuwait](/wiki/Kuwait "Kuwait") prior
to its release, with all preorders in the country being cancelled and
refunded.[68] No reason was given by Kuwaiti officials for the ban;[69]
publications speculated it was due to the game's [Gulf War](/wiki/Gulf_War
"Gulf War") setting.[70]

### Multiplayer beta

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Call_of_Duty:_Black_Ops_6&action=edit&section=10
"Edit section: Multiplayer beta")]

Those who pre-ordered _Black Ops 6_ or had an active subscription to Xbox Game
Pass received early access to an open
[beta](/wiki/Software_release_life_cycle#Beta "Software release life cycle")
test for the game's multiplayer component. The early access period took place
from August 30 to September 4, while a second period, available to all
players, began on September 6 and concluded on September 9.[71] Critic
impressions of _Black Ops 6_ 's beta were mostly positive;[72][73][74][75][76]
critics highlighted the omnidirectional movement system as a standout
feature,[74][72][73] but had mixed responses towards the game's map
design[73][76] and gunplay.[72][75]

Following the game's release, Treyarch supported _Black Ops 6_ with free

_Black Ops 6_ received "generally favorable reviews" from critics, according
to the [review aggregator](/wiki/Review_aggregator "Review aggregator")
website [Metacritic](/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic").[89]
[OpenCritic](/wiki/OpenCritic "OpenCritic") determined that 91% of critics
recommended the game.[90] Critics generally considered the title to be an
improvement over its direct predecessor, _[Call of Duty: Modern Warfare
III](/wiki/Call_of_Duty:_Modern_Warfare_III_\(2023_video_game\) "Call of Duty:
Modern Warfare III \(2023 video game\)")_ (2023);[92][91][94][95] some said it
was a return to form for the series.[94][95]

Reviewers had a generally positive response towards _Black Ops 6_ 's
campaign.[3][9][94] _IGN_ 's Simon Cardy gave it a 9/10 rating, writing that
it was a "hugely welcome reinvigoration" of the series.[3] _GameSpot_ 's Phil
Hornshaw praised the campaign's mission design and its cast of characters, but
felt "lost" during some parts of its narrative.[9] Conversely, _[PC
Gamer](/wiki/PC_Gamer "PC Gamer")_ 's Nova Smith considered the campaign to be
"thoroughly mediocre" and "tedious".[98] Some critics highlighted one campaign
mission, "Emergence", as a standout for its inclusion of [horror
elements](/wiki/Horror_game "Horror game") and aspects of [_Call of Duty_ 's
Zombies mode](/wiki/Call_of_Duty_Zombies "Call of Duty Zombies").[100][101]
_[PCGamesN](/wiki/PCGamesN "PCGamesN")_ 's Lauren Bergin wrote that the
inclusion of zombies was a "perfect throughline that connects somewhat
disparate modes" and that it was "outright cool to experience."[100]
_[GamesRadar+](/wiki/GamesRadar%2B "GamesRadar+")_ 's Andrew Brown described
"Emergence" as _Black Ops 6_ 's most "subversive" level and felt its horror
elements provided "moments of quiet unease" that he did not expect from a
_Call of Duty_ level.[101]

The multiplayer component received praise from critics.[4][93][99]
_[VG247](/wiki/Gamer_Network "Gamer Network")_ 's Fran Ruiz wrote that _Black
Ops 6_ 's multiplayer was "an absolute blast to play", and that it was the
"most tight and polished the series has felt in more than a decade."[99] _IGN_
's Seth G. Macy praised the game's selection of maps, its gunplay, and the
omnidirectional movement system, but felt the latter did not "necessarily help
[him] competitively except in very specific situations."[4] _GameSpot_ 's
Hornshaw also praised the omnidirectional movement, stating that it creates "a
really high degree of fluidity", but offered criticism towards the
multiplayer's [respawn system](/wiki/Spawning_\(video_games\) "Spawning
\(video games\)"), which he felt was negatively affected by the "cramped"
design of the game's maps.[93] Both _GamesRadar+_ 's Luke Kemp and _[Digital
Trends](/wiki/Digital_Trends "Digital Trends")_ 's Billy Givens liked the
game's perk system, with the latter writing that he appreciated the need to
"consider the risk and rewards of choosing or abandoning perks [he'd]
typically rolled with in previous games."[91][94]

The Zombies mode was also met with positive reviews; critics liked the mode's
return to its round-based gameplay format, as opposed to the mode's [open
world](/wiki/Open_world "Open world") design in _Modern Warfare
III_.[97][99][102][96] _IGN_ 's Will Borger gave Zombies an 8/10 rating,
stating that the mode is "absurd and campy and amazing and goofy in all the
right ways"; he praised the mode's launch maps, "Terminus" and "Liberty
Falls", and its hidden quests and [easter eggs](/wiki/Easter_egg_\(media\)
"Easter egg \(media\)"), but disliked the "deeply annoying" dialogue for its
characters.[96] _GamesRadar+_ 's Brown also praised the launch maps, and
stated that _Black Ops 6_ 's version of Zombies revitalized his love for the
mode as a whole.[102] _[The Guardian](/wiki/The_Guardian "The Guardian")_ 's
Keith Stuart wrote that Zombies was "fraught and incredibly stressful" but
said that it was "a real blast" with friends.[97] _VG247_ 's Ruiz felt Zombies
"greatly benefited" from the omnidirectional movement system.[99]

Following the release of the "Season 1 Reloaded" game update in December 2024,
some players began accusing Activision and the developers of using [generative
artificial intelligence](/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence "Generative
artificial intelligence") for several in-game items, including custom [loading
screens](/wiki/Loading_screen "Loading screen"), calling cards, and
[emblems](/wiki/Emblem "Emblem"), and for artwork related to events in the
Zombies mode;[103][104] in particular, players highlighted a loading screen
that depicted a zombified [Santa Claus](/wiki/Santa_Claus "Santa Claus"),
which featured six fingers on one of his hands and other irregularities.[103]
Due to a requirement from [Valve](/wiki/Valve_Corporation "Valve
Corporation"), Activision updated _Call of Duty HQ_ 's
[Steam](/wiki/Steam_\(service\) "Steam \(service\)") page in January 2025 to
disclose that generative AI tools are used to "help develop some in-game
assets".[105] _[The Gamer](/wiki/Valnet "Valnet")_ 's Andrew King and
_[Inverse](/wiki/Inverse_\(website\) "Inverse \(website\)")_ 's Trone Dowd
condemned Activision for its usage of generative AI in _Black Ops 6_
;[106][107] the latter felt it was "doubly upsetting" due to the firings of
many 2D artists during [Microsoft's layoffs at Xbox and Activision Blizzard in
2024](/wiki/2022%E2%80%932025_video_game_industry_layoffs#Microsoft_Gaming
"2022–2025 video game industry layoffs").[107]

### Sales

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Call_of_Duty:_Black_Ops_6&action=edit&section=13
"Edit section: Sales")]

_Black Ops 6_ achieved the largest launch weekend in the franchise's
history,[108] and was the [best-selling video game in the United
States](/wiki/List_of_best-selling_video_games_in_the_United_States_by_year
"List of best-selling video games in the United States by year") in 2024.[109]
Microsoft's CEO [Satya Nadella](/wiki/Satya_Nadella "Satya Nadella") noted
high player engagement on release day and an increase in new Game Pass
subscriptions within a single day. Sales on PlayStation and
[Steam](/wiki/Steam_\(service\) "Steam \(service\)") increased by 60% compared
to _Modern Warfare III_.[108] By July 2025, _Black Ops 6_ reached 50 million
players.[110] According to [Circana](/wiki/Circana "Circana"), _Black Ops 6_
is—within the United States—the fifth highest-grossing PlayStation game of all
time, the eleventh best-selling title overall,[111] and is the best-selling
PlayStation 5 game since the console's launch in 2020.[112]
